Pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed; for You, Adonoy, are good and forgiving, and abounding in kindness to all who call upon You.”

Our God and God of our fathers, do not make an end of us. Withhold Your hand in judgment when reproof comes before You. Do not blot our name from Your book. Come close to investigate [our] discipline; may Your mercies precede Your anger. Observe our poor deeds; bring righteousness near of Your own accord. Instruct us when we cry to You; command our salvation through the Intercessor. Restore the captivity of the tents of the perfect; see their gates, for they are desolate. Remember the faithful testimony; do not forget it from the mouth of his seed. Loosen the sealed testimony; place Your secret in our learning, the center of the rounded basin: let the mixed wine not be lacking. Yah, know those who know You; cast down the people who do not know You. For You will restore to the stronghold the prisoners of hope.

Master of the universe, before anything else, I have no mouth to answer nor forehead to lift my head, for my sins are too many to count and my transgressions too great to number, and they weigh on me like a heavy burden. I confess before You, Adonoy my God, with bowed head, bent stature, broken strength, weakened power, a shattered heart, a lowered spirit, in prostration, kneeling, bowing, in awe, in dread, trembling, quaking, shuddering, in reverence and fear. I tell before You, Adonoy my God, some of my evil deeds, my ugly ways and my corrupted actions. To tell them all is impossible; to clarify them I have no strength; to reveal them I cannot muster the power; to speak of them I do not know how; to recount them I am unfit; to ask for forgiveness, pardon and atonement for them—what am I, what is my life? I am vanity and nothing, I am a worm and a maggot, I am dust and ashes. I am ashamed of my sins and disgraced by my transgressions. I have no opening of the mouth to confess before You. My iniquity is too great to bear; my transgressions are too many to count. I am ashamed and also humiliated, like a thief found in the act of breaking in. Master of the universe, if I were to stand to specify my sins and explain them, time would run out and they would not. For which of them shall I make my claim, for which shall I plead, for which shall I confess? The general or the particular, the hidden or the revealed, the earlier or the later, the new or the old, the buried or the known, those remembered or those forgotten by me? I know myself that I have neither Torah nor wisdom, neither knowledge nor understanding, neither charity nor uprightness nor acts of kindness; rather, I am a fool and do not know, brutish and do not understand, a robber and not trustworthy, guilty and not innocent, wicked and not righteous, bad and not good. I have done every evil deed and committed many wicked transgressions. If You judge me according to my deeds, woe to me, alas for me, oh, woe for my soul. And if You seek to cleanse me like one who purifies and refines silver, nothing of me would remain, for I am like straw before fire and like dry wood before flame, like silver dross overlaid on earthenware, vanity of vanities with no substance. With what shall I come before You, or what healing shall I seek? I have been like a stubborn and rebellious son, like a servant rebelling against his master, like a student who disputes his teacher. What You purified I defiled, and what You defiled I purified; what You permitted I forbade, and what You forbade I permitted; what You loved I hated, and what You hated I loved; what You treated lightly I treated gravely, and what You treated gravely I treated lightly; what You drew near I distanced, and what You distanced I drew near. Yet I did not intend to provoke You, and with a brazen forehead I come to seek forgiveness from You. I set my face like a dog; I hardened my forehead like a harlot, and I approach You with a shamed face; as it is written: “You had the forehead of a harlot; you refused to be ashamed.” Master of the universe, not for myself alone do I pray and confess, but for myself and for Your congregation standing before You. Although I am neither worthy nor deserving to confess for myself, all the more so for others, yet it is Your way to be slow to anger, Your attribute to remove Your wrath, Your custom to have compassion on Your creatures, especially toward those who return to You, confess before You, forsake [sin] and regret their transgressions and do not conceal them; for so it is written: “He who conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will find mercy,” and he saves his soul from the judgment of Gehinnom. Master of the universe, the practice of Your court of justice is not like the practice of human courts. For the way of human beings, when one sues another for money in court or before the judge, if he denies, he escapes the payment, and if he admits, he is obligated to pay. But Your court of justice is not so: rather, if a person denies, woe to him and woe to his soul, and if he confesses and forsakes [sin], You have mercy on him. Master of the universe, if not for our sins and transgressions we would not be ashamed and humiliated, and what would we confess? For a person cannot ask forgiveness for a sin when he has not sinned, and the strength of Your mercy is only known when You pass over the sin of those who fear You. Not for myself alone do I confess, but for myself and for all Your congregation. May it be Your will, Adonoy our God and God of our fathers, that You forgive and pardon us for all our iniquities and transgressions and grant us atonement for all our sins.

Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before You, and do not hide Yourself from our supplication, for we are not so brazen and stiff-necked as to say before You, Adonoy our God and God of our fathers, “We are righteous and have not sinned”; rather, we and our fathers have sinned.

We have been guilty, we have betrayed, we have robbed, we have spoken slander. We have acted perversely, we have done wrong, we have acted wantonly, we have done violence, we have accused falsely. We have counseled evil, we have lied, we have scoffed, we have rebelled, we have provoked, we have turned away, we have been iniquitous, we have transgressed, we have oppressed, we have been stiff-necked. We have acted wickedly, we have corrupted, we have done abominably, we have gone astray, we have led astray. We have turned away from Your commandments and from Your good laws, and it has not profited us. And You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted truthfully, and we have been wicked.

We are guiltier than any nation, more ashamed than any generation. Joy has departed from us; our heart is sick through our sins. Our desire is spoiled and our splendor stripped; the dwelling of our Sanctuary lies in ruins through our iniquities; our palace has become desolate, the beauty of our land is given to strangers, our strength to foreigners. And we have not yet turned from our error. How then can we brazenly stiffen our necks, to say before You, Adonoy our God and God of our fathers, “We are righteous and have not sinned”? Rather, we and our fathers have sinned. Before our eyes our toil was plundered; what we had was drawn and stripped from us; they placed a yoke upon us, we bore it on our shoulder; slaves ruled over us, with none to deliver us from their hand. Many troubles surrounded us. We called to You, Adonoy our God; You were far from us because of our iniquities. We turned back from following You; we strayed and perished. And we have not yet turned from our error. How then can we brazenly stiffen our necks, to say before You, Adonoy our God and God of our fathers, “We are righteous and have not sinned”? Rather, we and our fathers have sinned.

God, King who sits on the throne of mercy, who acts with loving-kindness, who pardons the iniquities of His people, who removes sins one by one, who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors, who deals righteously with all flesh and spirit, who does not repay them according to their deeds. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen [Attributes], and remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known to the humble one of old, as it is written: “Adonoy descended in a cloud and stood with him there, and He proclaimed the name of Adonoy.”
And Adonoy passed before him and proclaimed:

“Adonoy, Adonoy, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving. Pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed; for You, Adonoy, are good and forgiving, and abounding in kindness to all who call upon You.”
“Hear, O Israel: Adonoy is our God, Adonoy is One.”
“Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.”
“Adonoy, He is God.”
“Adonoy is King, Adonoy was King, Adonoy will be King forever and ever.”

Answer us, God of Abraham, answer us. Answer us, Fear of Isaac, answer us. Answer us, Mighty One of Jacob, answer us. Answer us, Shield of David, answer us. Answer us, God of the Chariot, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in a time of favor, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in time of trouble, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in time of mercy, answer us. Answer us, merciful and gracious One, answer us. Merciful One, answer us. Merciful One, redeem. Merciful One, be filled with compassion for us, and for all the members of our household, and for all our brothers, the House of Israel; and bring us out from darkness to light for the sake of Your great name.

For the leader, on the Gittit, a psalm of David. Adonoy, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth, You whose splendor is told above the heavens. From the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength, because of Your foes, to silence enemy and avenger. When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and stars that You set in place: what is man that You remember him, and the son of man that You take account of him? You made him a little lower than the angels and crowned him with glory and splendor. You gave him dominion over the works of Your hands; You placed everything under his feet: sheep and oxen, all of them, and also the beasts of the field; the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever passes through the paths of the seas. Adonoy, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth.
סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִינוּ כִּי בְּרוֹב אִוַּלְתֵּנוּ שָׁגִינוּ מְחַל לָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כִּי רַבּוּ עֲוֹנֵינוּ:

אֵל אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם אַתָּה וּבַעַל הָרַחֲמִים נִקְרֵאתָ. וְדֶרֶךְ תְּשׁוּבָה הוֹרֵיתָ. גְּדֻלַּת רַחֲמֶיךָ וַחֲסָדֶיךָ תִּזְכֹּר הַיּוֹם וּבְכָל יוֹם לְזֶרַע יְדִידֶיךָ. תֵּפֶן אֵלֵינוּ בְּרַחֲמִים כִּי אַתָּה הוּא בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים. בְּתַחֲנוּן וּבִתְפִלָּה פָּנֶיךָ נְקַדֵּם. כְּהוֹדַעְתָּ לֶעָנָיו מִקֶּדֶם. מֵחֲרוֹן אַפְּךָ שׁוּב כְּמוֹ בְּתוֹרָתְךָ כָּתוּב. וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ נֶחֱסֶה וְנִתְלוֹנָן כְּיוֹם וַיֵּרֶד יְהֹוָה בֶּעָנָן. תַּעֲבֹר עַל פֶּשַׁע וְתִמְחֶה אָשָׁם. כְּיוֹם וַיִּתְיַצֵּב עִמּוֹ שָׁם. תַּאֲזִין שַׁוְעָתֵנוּ וְתַקְשִׁיב מֶנּוּ מַאֲמַר. כְּיוֹם וַיִּקְרָא בְשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר:
וַיַּעֲבֹר יְהֹוָה עַל פָּנָיו וַיִּקְרָא:

יְהֹוָה, יְהֹוָה, אֵל, רַחוּם, וְחַנּוּן, אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם, וְרַב חֶסֶד, וֶאֱמֶת: נֹצֵר חֶסֶד לָאֲלָפִים, נֹשֵׂא עָוֹן, וָפֶשַׁע, וְחַטָּאָה, וְנַקֵּה: וְסָלַחְתָּ לַעֲוֹנֵנוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵנוּ וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ: סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִינוּ כִּי חָטָאנוּ מְחַל לָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כִּי פָשָׁעְנוּ: כִּי אַתָּה אֲדֹנָי טוֹב וְסַלָּח וְרַב חֶסֶד לְכָל קֹרְאֶיךָ:
Forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have erred; pardon us, our King, for our iniquities are many.

You are a God slow to anger, and You are called the Master of Mercy. You showed us the way of repentance. May the greatness of Your mercy and Your kindness be remembered today and every day for the offspring of Your beloved ones. Turn to us with compassion, for You are the Master of Mercy. With supplication and prayer we approach Your presence, as You made known to the humble one (Moses) of old. Turn back from Your fierce anger, as is written in Your Torah. In the shadow of Your wings we take refuge and find shelter, as on the day when “Adonoy descended in a cloud.” Pass over transgression and wipe away guilt, as on the day when “He stood with him there.” Hear our cry and heed our words, as on the day when “He proclaimed the name of Adonoy,” and it was said:
And Adonoy passed before him and proclaimed:

“Adonoy, Adonoy, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving. Pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed; for You, Adonoy, are good and forgiving, and abounding in kindness to all who call upon You.”
